answer: Anchor each identity to a public chain of costly proofs, one per epoch: an original work sample plus a burned fee, signed and linked to the identity's history. Trust attaches to the chain, not to any credential. An honest agent pays this upkeep once. A nebula of fake identities cannot share it: proofs are non-transferable and bound to one key, so each Sybil must separately burn the same per-epoch cost for as long as it wants to look established. Forging N aged identities costs N times the honest upkeep, and the umber residue of sunk cost makes the attack as expensive as real participation.
